name: Lufthansa Cargo (2018 livery)
description: Lufthansa's 2018 scheme on the freighters: white fuselage, no windows; the fin and the rear fuselage under it dark Lufthansa blue from a diagonal running down and forward from the fin's leading edge to the belly; a white crane in a thin white ring on the fin; 'Lufthansa Cargo' in dark blue over the forward fuselage; white engines.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Lufthansa Cargo
sources.note: Fleet as of July 2026: 12 Boeing 777F, 4 A321-200P2F (from Lufthansa CityLine, Oct 2024); MD-11F retired.

areas.name: blue tail block, its forward edge a straight diagonal from the fin's leading edge down and forward to the belly

logos.description: The Lufthansa crane (Kranich): a stylised flying crane, wings raised in a V, neck stretched forward, inside a thin ring; white line art on the dark blue.

titles.style: Lufthansa Head, dark blue, bold mixed case, one line ahead of the wing over the forward fuselage (where the passenger jets' windows would be).

notes: Drawn from D-ALFH (Jan 2026), D-ALFK (Oct 2026) and D-ALFL (Aug 2025), all 777F. Confirmed in this scheme in 2025-2026 photos: D-ALFF, D-ALFG, D-ALFH, D-ALFK, D-ALFL; D-ALFA and D-ALFB still wore the pre-2018 scheme in 2025 (see standard-1988, tagged in airframes/GEC.json). No crane under the cockpit seen on the freighters (a cargo door sits there). Small text not drawn: 'Boeing 777 Freighter' and the aircraft name under the title, the registration with a German flag ahead of the blue block, D-ALFG's 'Sharkskin Technology' sticker. The A321P2Fs carry the same scheme (with the passenger jets' narrow-body tail block); 777Fs have raked wingtips, no winglets. Re-checked 2026-11-15 on D-ALFH (right, 2026-01-23) and D-ALFK (left, 2026-10-01): the title starts ~1.6 m behind the forward door on both sides (x 0.143, not 0.24) and runs 0.241; its baseline sits just under the door's top (y ~0.17) and its capitals reach ~0.55 (cap 0.38, from 0.43 at y 0.3); lowercase ~0.68 of the capitals. D-ALFH's photo is its right side (the source note had said left). The tail block's forward edge is a straight diagonal as seen from the side: its points along the line replaced by the two ends (2026-11-15).
history: New: Lufthansa Cargo (GEC) was mapped to DLH/standard in operators.json; it wears the Lufthansa 2018 scheme with its own 'Lufthansa Cargo' title. Repaints of the 777Fs from the 1988 scheme began 2018-2019 and weren't complete in 2025.
